post.summary: Analyze a change and trigger a release announcement
post.description:
Single-call entry point that generates the `analysisJson` internally from a
PR title + optional description and diff, then runs the full release flow.

Use this instead of `POST /api/v1/releases` when you do not want to pre-compute
the analysis JSON yourself. Works with or without a code diff.

**GitHub callers** — pass `prTitle`, `prDescription`, `diff` (optional) and any
GitHub context fields (`prNumber`, `branch`, `author`). The endpoint generates a
structured analysis and produces a customer-facing announcement email.

**Non-GitHub callers** — pass `title` and `description` instead. No diff required.

All other fields (`projectId`, `externalGroupIds`, `productId`, `sourceRepo`, `marketResearch`,
`generationMode`, `userFacing`, `html`, `subject`, `minimumHoursBetweenSends`) behave identically to `POST /api/v1/releases`.

prTitle.description: PR title — required for GitHub callers (use `title` for non-GitHub callers). One of prTitle or title must be supplied.
prTitle.example: Add webhook retry with exponential backoff

prDescription.description: PR description / body (optional but recommended for accuracy)

title.description: Release title — required for non-GitHub callers (use `prTitle` for GitHub callers). One of prTitle or title must be supplied.
title.example: Dark mode support for the dashboard

description.description: Release notes — non-GitHub alternative to prDescription

diff.description: Code diff (optional). Improves analysis accuracy when provided.

prNumber.description: PR number — stored as metadata, not required for analysis

author.description: PR author login — stored as metadata

version.description: Release version string (e.g. "v2.4.0") — attached to analysisJson

reviewer.description: PR reviewer login(s) — stored as metadata

clickupUrl.description: ClickUp ticket URL — stored as metadata

systemPrompt.description: Override the default AI analysis system prompt (CI callers use repo-specific prompt)

openApiSpec.description: Serialised OpenAPI paths+components JSON (capped at 60 KB server-side). Improves contract-impact detection.

peerManifests.description: Serialised peer repo manifests JSON (capped at 20 KB server-side). Used for blast-radius analysis.

analyzeOnly.description: When true, returns the analysisJson without creating a release record or sending any emails.

async.description:
When true, enqueues the analysis job and returns 202 with a `jobId` immediately.
Poll `GET /api/v1/releases/jobs/{jobId}` until `status` is `complete` or `failed`.
Requires `RELEASES_ANALYZE_QUEUE_URL` to be configured server-side (returns 503 if not).
When false (default), the call is synchronous — blocks until the LLM completes and returns 200.

200.description:
**Sync** (default, `async` omitted or `false`). Blocks until the LLM completes.
Announcement sent — or, when `analyzeOnly=true`, the analysis JSON is returned without any release created.

post.summary: Trigger a release announcement
post.description:
Generates an AI-written HTML email for a merged PR and sends it to the configured
contact group. Always requires authentication.

**productId**: required for all callers except the platform service account
(the account whose ID matches `MAILDRIP_INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ID`). When the platform
service account calls this endpoint without a `productId`, it defaults to `"maildrip"`.
All other accounts must supply `productId` explicitly or provide a `projectId` whose
stored project already has one.

**projectId shorthand**: pass `projectId` (from a previously created project or from
the first-run response) and `externalGroupIds`/`productId` become optional — the project supplies
them. Body params always override project defaults for the current call.

**First run**: omit `projectId` and provide `externalGroupIds` and `productId` directly. The
endpoint auto-creates a project and returns its `projectId` in the response — save it
as a CI secret for future calls.

**Template**: if the resolved project has a `templateId`, that template's HTML is
retrieved and passed to Claude as a design/brand reference. AI still generates the final
email but uses the template to inform layout and style.

analysisJson.description: The PR analysis JSON produced by the pr-merge-analysis workflow

projectId.description: Release Project ID — makes externalGroupIds/productId optional

externalGroupIds.description: Customer-facing contact groups. Required if projectId is not set.

productId.description: Product identifier. Required unless the caller is the platform service account, in which case it defaults to "maildrip". If projectId is supplied and the project already has a productId, this field is optional for all callers.

marketResearch.description: Pre-fetched market research text to ground AI copy in customer intelligence

generationMode.description:
Per-call override for email generation. `generate` — AI from scratch (default).
`revamp` — AI improves the html+subject draft you supply. `static` — no AI, html+subject used verbatim.
Falls back to the project's generationMode setting when omitted.

userFacing.description:
Explicit override for whether a customer-facing email is sent. When false, the release is saved
as status=internal and only the engineering notification (notify-team) fires. When omitted,
analysisJson.user_facing is consulted, then the project's defaultUserFacing, then defaults to true.

html.description: Required when generationMode is "static" or "revamp". The caller-supplied HTML body.

Send a transactional email
post.description: Send a transactional email to one recipient or a contact group. Supports optional AI revamp (dynamic mode) that rewrites your draft subject and body using a plain-language brief.

to.description: Recipient email address. Also accepted as 'email_address' for backwards compatibility. Required when group_ids is not provided.

group_ids.description: One or more contact group IDs. All group members receive the email. Members are deduplicated across groups. Can be combined with 'to' to add a one-off address alongside a group. Maximum 500 resolved recipients across all groups — use the campaign or instant-email API for larger audiences.

subject.description: Email subject line. When dynamic is true this is used as a content suggestion — the AI may rewrite it.

html.description: HTML body of the email. Use {{VARIABLE_NAME}} placeholders for per-recipient values (e.g. {{FIRST_NAME}}, {{ORDER_ID}}). When dynamic is true this is used as a content suggestion.
html.example: Hi {{FIRST_NAME}}, your order is on the way!

dynamic.description: Set to true to have AI rewrite your subject and html using 'context' as a brief. The AI preserves your brand voice and intent while improving clarity and engagement. Requires 'context'. AI sends are billed at 1 credit per 500 tokens used.

context.description: The brief passed to the AI. Can be a plain string ("Warm order confirmation, include urgency") or a structured object ({"tone": "warm", "urgency": "high", "product": "running shoes"}). Required when dynamic is true.
context.example: Post-purchase confirmation. Warm and professional tone.

variation.description:
Controls how AI generation is applied. Only meaningful when dynamic is true.
'shared' (default) — AI generates one email for the entire batch. Cost: 1 AI call regardless of recipient count.
'per_recipient' — AI generates a unique email per person, using their stored contact attributes as additional context. Capped at 50 recipients. Cost: 1 AI call per recipient.

variables.description: Global variable values injected into all recipients' emails. Use UPPERCASE_KEYS to match {{PLACEHOLDER}} syntax. Contact attributes stored via /api/v1/identify are automatically injected and take precedence over these globals.

personalizations.description: Per-recipient variable overrides for small sends (max 20). For larger groups, store attributes via POST /api/v1/identify — they are automatically injected at send time without being passed in every request.

data.description: Variable overrides for this recipient. Keys are merged over globals.

reply_to.description: Reply-To address. When set, replies from recipients go here instead of the sender.

cc.description: CC addresses. When sending to a group each member triggers a separate send, so CC recipients receive one copy per primary recipient. Credits: recipients × (1 + cc.length + bcc.length).

bcc.description: BCC addresses. Same billing behaviour as cc.

experiment.description: Optional A/B experiment. Each recipient is randomly bucketed into one variant according to the supplied weights. Omit to send without an experiment — existing behaviour is completely unchanged.

id.description: Caller-supplied experiment identifier. Auto-generated UUID if omitted.

metric.description: Reserved for the auto-promotion scoring job (not yet active). Accepted and stored but has no effect on the current send.

score_after_hours.description: Reserved for the auto-promotion scoring job (not yet active). Accepted and stored but has no effect on the current send.

auto_promote.description: Reserved for the auto-promotion scoring job (not yet active). Accepted but has no effect on the current send.

variants.description: Variant definitions. Weights must sum to 1.0 (±0.01 tolerance). Each variant supplies EITHER subject+html (static) OR context (AI-generated — requires dynamic: true on the request).

weight.description: Fraction of recipients assigned to this variant.

subject.description: Static subject for this variant (requires html).
subject.example: Act now — your renewal expires soon

html.description: Static HTML body for this variant (requires subject).

context.description: AI brief for this variant. Mutually exclusive with subject+html. Requires dynamic: true on the request.
